issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book], owner: String) (implying an owner parameter/property), but the reference solution implements init(books: [Book]) without an owner parameter. This mismatch between the specification and the solution will confuse students about the expected constructor signature and whether an owner property should exist. It can also cause tests (or student implementations following the spec) to fail if they rely on the owner parameter.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the artifacts consistent. Two options:

1) Align the solution and template to the problem statement: add a let owner: String property to Bookstore and change the initializer to init(books: [Book], owner: String). Update all places that create a Bookstore (e.g., assembleBookstore) to pass an owner value.

2) Or, if the owner parameter was not intended, update the problem statement to require init(books: [Book]) (and remove the owner parameter from the signature in the requirements). Option (1) is recommended because the problem currently explicitly asks for the owner parameter.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with signature init(books: [Book], owner: String) (i.e. the Bookstore concept includes an owner). The solution implementation of Bookstore (and the Client that constructs it) uses init(books: [Book]) and does not expose or store an owner. This mismatch between the problem description and the provided implementation creates confusion: students following the problem will implement or look for an initializer that accepts an owner, but the template/solution code uses a different initializer. This hinders the direct mapping from the requirement to the code and may cause students to waste time reconciling the missing parameter or to implement an incompatible initializer.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the artifacts consistent. Either (A) update the solution and template to match the problem by adding an owner property and initializer parameter:
- Add `let owner: String` to class Bookstore
- Change initializer to `init(books: [Book], owner: String)` and set `self.owner = owner`
- Update any call sites (e.g. Client.assembleBookstore()) to call `Bookstore(books: books, owner: "<owner name>")`.
Or (B) if the owner requirement was unintentional, update the problem statement to require `init(books: [Book])` (remove the owner parameter). Option A is preferable because the problem explicitly lists an owner parameter and instructs that fields should be `let` constants.
